description: Please contact Debbie at Ext. 222

Last spring we called you to report that our sump pump that in the past 50 years has been used to eject laundry water from the basement, was running continuously since February.  You came twice to check on it including taking a water sample and 'listening' at the street shut off valve.  You did not detect a leak.   Since then we have had three plumbers in to look at the problem.  We scoped the sewer line, one listened at the interior shut off, and we turned off the building water to see if it affected the pumping.  All negative.  The sump pump continues to run every 90 seconds 24/7, and we have one flood when the pump was accidentally turned off.  This current drought has not affected it either.   We are not sure what you can do but  we know that we have a constant source of water entering the sump, which one of the plumbers said would probably rule out a sewer line leak.  We are a 20 unit condo building.  This water is coming from somewhere, but our water bill suggests it is not an internal leak, as well as the other tests.  We thought you should know.

description: Dear Evanston Police department,  I'm writing as a former Northwestern student and Evanston resident to say that I am deeply disappointed in your department for how you treated Lawrence Crosby in the 2015 traffic stop. It is unfathomable to me that the use of excessive force was found to be justified. This innocent man was accused of stealing his car by a racist citizen who I'm sure meant to do good, but was mistaken. However, your officers could and should have worked to de-escalate and properly investigate the situation. Instead, you brutalized a brilliant and accomplished young man.   I do not feel safe in Evanston now that I know your officers react in this manner to situations that are not dangerous. I'm calling on you to fire the officers involved. I'm also calling on you to train your people (or re-train as the case may be) in nonviolent de-escalation methods of policing.   Evanston and Northwestern have such a rich relationship and history. Evanston itself is a beautiful and diverse community.  But the way your department treats people of color is unacceptable and is certainly making Northwestern a less safe place for students of color.  Please do not do this again.  Best, Tiernan

description: Dear Evanston Tenant Landlord Ordinance,  48 Hour Rule  First and foremost I thank you for your attention and hearing my professional position.  I request a formal hearing to discuss the 48 hour requirement for showings.  Poor policy and skewed: I believe the 48 hour showing notice is punitive to the property owners and  unnecessary. I understand that complaints of slum landlords entering  at will  was the etiology of this local policy to prevent such action and provide ample notice.  However, you are affecting the practice of licensed Realtors who have higher standard of care and a responsibility to show and sell properties.  You are basically taking away the hammer from  the carpenter when you don't permit timely showings which would be in a reasonable 24 hour notice.   Time is of the Essence: It places the property rights of Evanston property owners -clients in a harmful  position because you are losing potential prospects that cannot see the unit in the natural rhythm of the the 24 hour notice for showings that the Multiple Listing Service  is based on.    Anti-Competiton: You are directly blocking and preventing the sale and marketing of a property and it is Anti-competition and a potential Federal concern.    Practical: I encourage you to be more flexible with this issue.  As a Registered Nurse and Masters Social worker from the University of Chicago and 15 year Top Producer Real Estate Broker I feel I need to advocate for my clients. The 24 hour notice is the natural rhythm for a showing and places everyone on alert in the appropriate time and fashion.  I am confident that 90% of the Real Estate community would agree with me.  I have a particular situation at 1720 Maple unit 4th floor, Evanston, Illinois 60201 where the tenant has blocked my showings even with 48 hour notice.   If I can't show... I can't sell !     Michael Marin MA,MSW,RN Managing Broker-Top Producer Signature Homes Realty,inc 847-312-1014

category: Ask A Question / Send A Message
description: A resident, Dr. Kate Zilla, has an issue with the utility wires near her home. She has contacted Mayor Tisdahl and Wally about her dissatisfaction with the appearance of the wires and the possibility of hazardous conditions. She has contacted ComEd and ATT, but had no luck in getting the situation resolved.  I met with Dr. Zilla on 1/27/16 to discuss issues and take photographs (see network folder: P:\Oscar\2421 Brown Avenue - Wire Pics). I let her know that the issue would be relayed to our Public Works Director for review of potential hazardous conditions and to contact our staff liaisons at ComEd and ATT about dressing the wires properly now and for any future additions.  For more information, see resident's original email:  Hi Mayor Tisdahl, First of all, I want to thank you for facilitating the 7th ward meeting at the Civic Center last night. It was really helpful to hear from all the candidates who were there, and for the rest of us to have the opportunity to speak up about our visions and concerns as well. Thanks too for encouraging me to email you about my specific problem concerning the growing number of cable and electric wires that are ending up on the pole outside of the coach house I own, and that sits on an alley, away from the street. Background   Specifically, I own a small coach house on 2421 Brown Ave., and am part of a small condo association there. Long ago the maple tree on the alley next to my home of 17 years was cut down, replaced by a telephone/electric pole. Over the years, there weren’t that many wires. But within the last few years, not only Com Ed had wires, but more and more cable wires started going up.   The ‘growth’ of these wires has become seemingly exponential and really egregious in the last 18 months-2 years. What was once a few wires has now become somewhere around 24 total (and counting). This has made me very unhappy, in part because as a person nearing retirement, I know this will likely affect my property values. But even more so, I no longer enjoy just coming home after a long, hard day at work, unless I don’t look up at what I call an ugly mess, one that is with me 24/7. (Please see picture below, after wires were 'cleaned up'.) Others agree, including some of those below.  Attempted solutions I’ve talked to and tried to find solutions with the following: my condo association (4-5 wires come from our main building) City of Evanston: 311, plus searching the 311 city website (and tried Ald. Grover - she never responded) Comm. Ed.: their regular and regional rep (‘if you have $100,000. you can bury them’ - but did get some of the wires 'cleaned up') Cable: Comcast (many calls and multiple people, and visit by my regular cable guy - 'nothing you can do') ATT (many calls, multiple people)   Of all the companies and individuals I contacted above, I have to say probably the most disappointing was Jane Glover’s non-response. Fairly recently, I tried her home number, listed on the city website, a couple of times and left messages – but to no avail; she never called back.   Currently, in addition to wires coming from my condo association's main building (and we’re continuing to explore ‘bundling’ our cable providers), AT&T and Comcast wires are also coming from the house across the alley (I spoke to them, they seemed amenable), at least two other houses down the block (through back yards), and my next door neighbor (I spoke with her, she also seemed amenable). A second pole on the alley and Brown Ave., on the other side of my home, also has ‘fatter’ bundled wires, but is less unsightly. Thanks very much for listening, and for any help you can give.   Kate Zilla

Another concern about bus service along Dempster Street is the planned addition of PULSE bus service.  With only limited stops, the high schoolers will have farther to walk to a bus stop. Therefore, the 250 Dempster Street bus does not sound like a viable alternative to get to and from ETHS.  Riders living near Church Street can now take the 208 Church Street bus to Old Orchard or Downtown Evanston for work, shopping, and entertainment.  They can’t get to Old Orchard or Jewel for grocery shopping on the 250 Dempster Street bus.  Many riders along the 208 route are elderly and would not be able to physically get to Dempster or Golf for the proposed alternate buses. description: Hello, Our Company eCycle Solutions would like to help the community by setting up a recycling drive for old electronics, so people of your community could easily drop off what they don't use but they just can't throw in the garbage.  We are a responsible electronics recycling and asset recovery company based out of the Chicago-land area. Computers and other electronics are becoming obsolete at a faster rate every day. Many organizations landfill their unused or non-working IT related equipment. The State of Illinois has passed a law banning all electronics from landfills which has taken effect on January 1st, 2012. Other states such as Indiana, Michigan, and Wisconsin have also passed a similar law banning electronics from landfills. Putting electronics equipment into a landfill causes many issues both short term and long term due to the equipment’s composure of hazardous materials. Electronic waste consists of many components such as lead, mercury, cadmium, and other toxic and hazardous components.  This is where eCycle Solutions comes into play. Our company provides a responsible, environmentally friendly, secure, and an easy way to dispose of your obsolete and unwanted IT related equipment.  The only cost we have to apply is to those that are recycling old tube T.V's ($25 each) and old computer monitors ($10 each) All other electronics are accepted at no charge. For hosting this event our company will wave our pickup fee of $150 for your organization and supply a Pallet with a container to store the recycled electronics. Thank you for taking the time to read this through, let us start helping the community together. As an Evanston resident living at 2212 McDaniel Ave (SW corner of McDaniel and Noyes), and as the District 65 PTA Child Safety and Welfare Chair, I have spoken to numerous adjacent neighbors about the need for a 4-way stop at this busy intersection. My neighbor said she requested a stop sign from the City of Evanston a couple of years ago but was turned down because of the slight bend in the road on McDaniel just north of Noyes and the rationale that it does not give drivers enough time to see the stop sign were it to be installed. This issue could easily be mitigated by posting a  4-way stop ahead  sign for cars heading south on McDaniel, just before the bend in the road. The small measure of installing a four-way stop at this location would increase safety for both drivers and pedestrians.   Thank you for your consideration. FACTS from the Center for Aerosol Impacts on Climate and the Environment:  Aerosols and Human Health  Aerosol particles can contribute to a variety of human health problems. Particulate matter affects the health of more people than any other pollutant worldwide. According to estimates from the World Health Organization (WHO), particle pollution contributes to approximately 7 million premature deaths each year, making it one of the leading cause of worldwide mortality.1           The health effects of the particles are directly related to their size.2 Particles greater than 100 μm are generally too large to be inhaled. Particles between 10-100 μm can be inhaled, but are usually stopped by our body’s “filters”—the mucus membranes in our respiratory system. The term inhalable particles typically refers to particles less than 10 μm in size that can make it past the body’s defenses and deep into the lungs.  Inhalable coarse particles are particles between 2.5 and 10 μm in diameter (PM10) and are typically found near highways and factories. As the figure to the right shows, these particles are usually deposited in the nose, pharynx, and larynx.                  Fine particles have a diameter less than 2.5 μm (PM2.5) and are typically found in smoke and smog. These particles make it deeper into the lungs; a significant proportion of these fine particles are deposited in the trachea, bronchioles, and alveoli.

To add to this, on rainy days when everyone drives like it's the apocalypse, traffic is backed up all the way through this intersection because there's no stoplight.  I've asked about putting a light here before, and the answer I received was something like,  We've tested, and there isn't enough volume of traffic to justify this.   What, the cars just *disappear* after Lake and reappear at Davis?    I wish someone would tell me how to do that because the increasing number of people crossing at Grove to go to Roycemore and Dewey sure could use some help getting across this legal crosswalk.  (And yes, I know it's unmarked and they can  go around  to the lights, but try telling that to a parent with a 5 year old, wearing snow boots a size too big, in a city where it's winter at least 1/3 of the year.)

Fortunately, there's time to fix this!

description: I am trying to figure out why in the world the city would sound the emergency alarm at 10 or 11 at night because of a Cubs victory. It seems like such a misguided attempt.  There are thousands of people who do not follow baseball and don't check the city's website or facebook page that will be alarmed by the emergency alarms going off without any signs of an emergency. Beyond that there are thousands of children trying to get a good nights sleep to prepare for school tomorrow that will be woken up and scared. My son is one of them. In addition to being a young child, he has a strong phobia of alarms. He gets extremely scared and anxious when he hears them. It should be a wonderful evening if the Cubs win, I will get to spend my evening trying to calm my child down and get him back in bed so he can function at school. So should I keep him up extremely late in order to help him if the alarms go off or should I send him to bed only to be woken in a panic because the alarms are going off. Neither is a good solution, nor one I should have to make.  I am sure this sounded like a great idea around the meeting room but this misguided celebration will be my and unfortunately my sons nightmare evening. I hope the Cubs win but I am more hopeful you will see the impact of using the emergency alarm signal will have on my and I am positive many more family's around Evanston.

I am writing concerning a long-standing problem experienced by me and many other Evanston residents when we get heavy snows. Typically, when snow plows clear the side streets they also create a wall of snow at each end of our alleys. This often makes it impossible to get in or out of an alley without getting stuck, due to the fact that passenger vehicles do not have sufficient clearance to get through the snow banks created by the snow plows. This policy by the Department of Streets and Sanitation seems highly thoughtless and irresponsible, and puts people like myself at risk of suffering a heart attack or stroke by having to deal with trying to extricate their vehicles from the snow banks once they become stuck. I am hereby pleading and requesting that the snow plows avoid creating this serious situation in the future in order to ensure the health and safety of all Evanston residents who are subjected to the consequences of snow-blocked alleys.

Any road closure beyond December 31st, 2016 for the construction is a taking of property and residents’ right to use the road and reliance on the road for convenience and normal livelihood. The affected residents are from 1570 Elmwood Ave and more. Should the road be closed beyond December 31, 2016, then Evanston residents must be compensated for taking a road beyond a usual length. This is a reasonable request since there has been no weather delays that should extend the road closure beyond December 31, 2016. Had the construction company known that it would take beyond December 31, 2016 then it should have requested a permit beyond December 31, 2016 and the city should have provided advance notice to the residents as well. Had the construction company known that it would take longer than December 31, 2016 but did not disclose such intent or conceal a material fact then the construction company has committed a fraudulent act against the city of Evanston and its residents. Consequently, the city (on behalf of the residents that it serves) must take action against the construction.   The construction has further done damage to the city. I am pleading as a resident that the city take a serious look at the destruction and damages on behalf of its residents and taxpayers:  - First, the construction (sometimes starting before 7 am because the crew is getting ready) has violated city ordinance on the start time for construction which includes the time needed for the crew to get ready and thus has created nuisance to nearby residents. The nuisance both in noise and poor air quality by the creation of dust without proper gear to block it from nearby residents effectively has created a public hazard.  - Second, the construction has destroyed the trees and greens by the train tracks that keep the air clean by pouring cement onto the street and the trees without proper guarding, which is a destruction of public property.  - Third, cement trucks have been driving around the city of Evanston as if it is a highway at one point getting involved in an accident that killed a student from Northwestern University on a bike. The city roads are not a construction site and they are guests of our beautiful city so it is expected that all construction related vehicles should act with caution not without disregard for citizens and road rules.  - Fourth, a gas pipe burst right next to the construction site on Maple Ave after the construction dug up the street, which ComEd had to spend 2 days to repair.   As a resident I am exercising my right granted by the US Constitution, IL Constitution, and IL statutes to make the following requests to the City of Evanston. I first request a public hearing and notify all residents should the city decide to grant an extension of the road closure permit. The city has a legal obligation to review any taking of property right. Also, I request that the city review all nuisance violations and destruction of city property by the construction. Lastly, I request that the city review all safety precautions by the construction given the accident of a student death and gas pipe bursting.  Thank you.

description: Regarding Resolution 27-R-13, Authorizing the City of Evanston Establish a Moratorium on the Use of Unregulated Drone Technology:  From the text of this resolution, it appears that the primary concern driving the adoption of the moratorium on the use of unmanned aerial systems was the lack of cohesive regulations at a state and federal level. In the years following this resolution, Illinois has passed the  Freedom from Drone Surveillance Act,  which  states that a  law enforcement agency may not use a drone to gather information.  Further, the FAA has introduced extensive regulations regarding the use of drones, effectively treating them as any other aircraft. In light of the regulations that have been established at the state and local level, I believe that the concerns of resolution 27-R-13 have largely, if not entirely, been addressed.  I am a graduate student at Northwestern University and am involved in robotics research, and I can state that I have experienced several instances in which I wished to pursue a line of research, but the moratorium has prevented me from pursuing said research. I understand that there are still real and persistant concerns regarding the use of drones, but I feel that the moratorium, as it stands, is too strict, and prevents useful and meaningful use of these devices.  I ask that the city council consider amending this resolution in light of recent state and national regulations in order to allow the reasonable and responsible use of unmanned aerial systems within Evanston. While I do not have a background in city regulations, I feel that requiring the drone operator to obtain a license and to have the license on their person whenever operating an unmanned aerial system would address lingering concerns while not putting undue burden on those who wish to operate their systems in a safe and responsible manner.  Please do not hesitate to contact me at petrasswissler2022@u.northwestern.edu

eft a message there today.  Below you will find 10 picture I took during my visit to Steak and Shake on Oakton on this beautiful Easter Sunday afternoon. I was at Home Depot shopping for gardening supplies and decided to stop and get a milkshake (don't tell my family, I'm lactose intolerant and only get ice cream on special occasions). I pulled into the drive through and noticed that there was garbage and cigarette buts just discarded there, in piles. I pulled up a little further and looked under the takeout window, it was covered in a gooey substance (old milkshakes?) and trash that was stuck into the gunk, there was even an inhaler right under the window. It was months of grossness. I called the manager to the window and yelled that it was disgusting and i was taking pictures and sending them to the city. I parked and walked around the whole store documenting the mess including in their dumpster area, which featured overflowing garbage, garbage on the ground, birds and squirrels were visiting while i was there. I bet it hasn't been cleaned in months.  On behalf of independent and family restaurants everywhere, please do your best to not only sight the business for the garbage, but please also send an emergency health inspection as soon as possible. It has been my experience working in the food industry, that if it is a mess outside, it's even worse inside. I recently managed a cafe in Rogers Park for 3 years, it was in my job description to make sure the outside was swept every morning. Even more recently I spent the last year serving lunch at Dave's New Kitchen and helping Dave get set up. He would never allow trash outside, he or his wife Ellen can be found most mornings cleaning up outside personally, whether it's sweeping, keeping the sidewalk clear of snow or even making the parkway part of their duties and plant all sorts of nice flowers in the few beds on the block. Steak and Shake as a corporation, doesn't seem to care about the cleanliness of Evanston. They are making a profit here and yet do not follow the rules. I know I am not the first one to complain about this particular issue with this particular restaurant, part of why I'm so mad.  This is unacceptable for any business anywhere, let alone in Evanston.  I plan to share these pictures publicly and with Steak and Shake Corporate.  https://goo.gl/photos/M48myjnRrgRfRcRF7   Keep Evanston Beautiful!  Thanks for your attention!  Sincerely,  Josh Newman 811 Gaffield Pl. Evanston, IL 60201 847-452-2884 JNew81@gmail.com

description: Now that the traffic signals at the Emerson/Green Bay Rd/Ridge Ave. intersection seems complete, I would like to suggest something to prevent a problem with left turns onto Green Bay Rd.  and Emerson St. from northbound Ridge Ave. Currently, there are left turn directions painted on the pavement on Ridge, indicating which left turn lane is to be used for turning onto Emerson only, and which lane to be used only for turning left onto Green Bay Rd. This is fine, as long as the pavement is clear and these directions are readable.  However, come wintertime, when this pavement on Ridge may be covered and obscured by snow and ice, drivers may not be able to read these on-the-road left turn lane instructions. I suggest you put left turn signs on the existing overhead traffic lights, One on the left signal indicating that that leftmost lane is for turning onto Emerson only, and a sign on the right signal, indicating that that right lane is for turning onto Green Bay Rd. only.  This should be an easy fix; and drivers will then have left turn instructions, on both the pavement and up on the traffic signal, for which lane to use for Emerson and Green Bay Rd.  Even now, with the pavement lettered instructions, drivers still try to cut over from the Emerson left turn lane onto the lane for Green Bay Rd. and often cut-off drivers proceeding in the lane onto Green Bay Rd. This is dangerous and has or will cause accidents, especially in snowy/icy conditions.  I would be interested in hearing what you think of this idea.

This does nothing to address the problem of plastic bags in the trees, on the streets, in the sewage system and in the blue bin  recycling program where they jam up separation equipment at the Groot facility. description: I am writing regarding an “Abandoned Auto” sticker placed on my car by Officer Samson #105 on Wednesday, February 7, 2018.  My silver 2002 Lexus LS 430 was parked in front of my house at 1012 Mulford Street to where it is registered.  The auto had been used by my wife to go to the store as recently as the day before, Tuesday, February 6th.  According to the Abandon Auto sticker my vehicle must be removed from the entire block and not parked on either side of the street.  But my car has a displayed valid parking permit to park on my street, which is otherwise restricted parking.  According to the Evanston Police Department website, if a vehicle is reported abandoned “An officer will check the vehicle to determine if has been abandoned and make every effort to contact the registered owner to explain parking laws and city ordinances.” As my car was parked in front of my house all the officer needed to do was to ring my doorbell to confirm the car has not been abandoned and had recently been moved.  As I have been home ill with the flu for the past 10 days, there has always been someone at home to answer the door or phone or return a voicemail message.  I contacted 311 and advised them of the facts.  The woman, Beverly, informed me that there was a report of a gold Lexus at 1207 Mulford.  That is the other side of Barton, not even near my house.  My car not only is registered to 1012 Mulford, the same address where it was parked, but it has a vanity license plate with my name on it.  Contacting the registered owner could not have been easier but no effort was made.  Given the absolute lack of any effort by the officer to investigate this matter I have strong concern that the City might just as haphazardly tow my authorized and legally parked vehicle from in front of my home.   I would appreciate the Evanston Police Department recognition of the error and assurance that it will not attempt to remove my legally parked vehicle from the street in front of my house.

description: Hi,  We're in the process of putting together a national database of fire hydrant locations that will be used by insurance companies to better determine the appropriate rate for property and casualty insurance.  We've already compiled over 2.9 million hydrants including a growing portion of Illinois and I'd like to add yours to the mix.  I know that this information is already given to Verisk/ISO so they can rate your fire stations.  Is it possible to get this information from you?    You can see our application consumer facing application at www.freehomerisk.com.  Hydrants will be added to the return at the end of March and we'd love to have yours in there.  We combine the hydrant location with the distance to the local fire station to automatically determine the Fire Protection Class of every property in your city. It's one of the most important and asked questions -  how far is the nearest hydrant?  Our goal is to automate that process.  If you have hydrant locations in shapefile or geodatabase format that would be excellent.  You can see sort of how the tool would work on our website, www.hazardhub.com under the Tools tab.  We have distance to fire station and distance to fire hydrant will be similar.  As you will see we are not charging for this application.  We are not interested in anything that could be considered sensitive information.  Just the hydrant locations.  The same information we could gather driving down the streets of your town.  Places in Illinois that have graciously provided us with hydrants include: Lake County, Naperville, Homewood, Park Forest, East Moline, Shiloh, O'Fallen, Gurnee, Warrenville, and Tinley Park.   Some other places from around the country that have provided hydrants include: Washington DC, Boston, New York, Atlanta, Miami, Seattle, Minneapolis, Houston, San Diego, Los Angeles, Seattle, Portland, Denver, Hartford, Pittsburgh, Cleveland, and Baltimore. category: Ask A Question / Send A Message
description: This question is actually about parking ~ I didn't see that option. Tonight I was told by the parking monitor that I deserved a parking ticket while sitting in my car, because I had not put money in the meter. Is this true? Since when? Is this true for everyone? I work as a courier in the evenings, as do quite a few other people in Evanston--it's getting to be a lot, between the delivery companies and the rideshare companies, too. The understanding is that we will hang out in parking spaces between jobs, so that the people actually doing a pickup/dropoff can use the loading zones. Even if we tried to always sit in loading zones, there are not nearly enough for us, and that would lengthen job times for all of us. When we pull into a parking space, we have no idea how long we will be there for--It could truly be 30 seconds or, on a slow night, an hour. If we really do have to pay, we would try to pay as little as possible, probably putting in a nickel every 6 minutes, which seems ridiculous. What if it's raining or snowing? We need to go back and forth to the meter constantly? None of us doing these jobs has extra money -- putting a quarter in every time we pull in, then setting an alarm for 15 minutes just in case...would add up, and also seems silly. If the issue is that those of us working jobs are actually costing Evanston parking money, perhaps we could create a monthly parking pass one could purchase, something we could put in our rear window, that would allow us to sit in a car at an unpaid meter.  I (and, I'm sure, we) would love to work something out--Please let me know what the regulations actually are and whether you also have some win-win ideas! Thank you, Gwynneth
